why: I read both verifier checks against the words of their expect lines. Check 2 holds. "Documents --tsv" reasonably covers needing the README to mention the flag and say what it does. Check 1 breaks the criterion. Its expect line only asks that `--tsv` read tab-separated stdin and print the same JSON array that CSV mode prints for the same table. Its PASS condition adds two things the words don't force. First, it requires "both commands exit 0", and the expect line says nothing about exit codes. Second, it requires the output to equal one fixed array, "expected: [{\"name\":\"ann\",...}]". That checks the CSV parser's own result, when the words only ask for TSV output to match CSV output. Its FAIL condition likewise fails on "either command exits non-zero". These extra tests belong under Advisory, not in PASS/FAIL.
